key_insight: GAC-PINN improves PINN accuracy on sharp-gradient PDEs by combining geometry-adaptive sampling, boundary-constraint hardening, spectral feature mapping, and automatic constraint routing.
engineering_relevance: The framework is useful for high-fidelity simulation of stiff, localized phenomena in computational physics and applied mechanics where standard PINNs struggle with convergence and boundary enforcement.
method: Gradient-driven adaptive grid mapping concentrates points near steep features while keeping the map diffeomorphic via Jacobian regularization.
Adaptive bandwidth hard constraints enforce boundary conditions with spatially varying transition widths to reduce constraint conflicts.
Gaussian Fourier features and an operator-aware router boost high-frequency representation and choose the right hard-constraint form for time-dependent vs. steady PDEs.
evidence_signal: Across Burgers, sharp-peaked Poisson, and Allen-Cahn benchmarks, the method achieved very low relative L2 errors of about 1.75e-4, 2.87e-5, and 1.76e-3, outperforming baselines; ablations also showed AGM outperforms RAR unless paired with Fourier features.
watch_item: The multi-stage training and coupled modules may increase implementation complexity and require careful tuning to keep adaptive sampling and constraint enforcement stable.
paper_title: GAC-PINN: Geometry-Adaptive and Constraint-Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks
